purpose: Senna is used to relieve constipation, which means it helps you have a bowel movement when you are having trouble going to the bathroom. It is also sometimes used to clean out your bowels before a medical procedure or colonoscopy. It works within a few hours to get things moving again.
how_it_works: Senna contains natural compounds called sennosides that irritate the lining of your intestines in a gentle way. This irritation causes your intestines to squeeze and push stool through more quickly. It also helps draw water into your intestines, which softens the stool and makes it easier to pass.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects are stomach cramps, bloating, and gas. You may also notice your urine turning a yellowish or reddish-brown color, which is harmless. Diarrhea can happen if you take too much.
warnings: Do not use senna for more than one week unless your doctor tells you to, because long-term use can make your bowels dependent on it. Avoid it if you have severe stomach pain, nausea, vomiting, or a bowel blockage. Talk to your doctor before using it if you are pregnant, breastfeeding, or have a chronic condition like Crohn's disease or irritable bowel syndrome.
typical_dosing: For adults, the typical dose is 1 to 2 tablets (or 15 to 30 mg of sennosides) taken once or twice a day, usually at bedtime. It generally works within 6 to 12 hours. Always follow the directions on the package or what your doctor or pharmacist tells you.
